content: Clobetasone, also known by its International Nonproprietary Name (INN), is a corticosteroid primarily utilized in dermatology for the treatment of inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, and various forms of dermatitis. It is also used in ophthalmology for specific eye-related conditions. When applied topically as clobetasone butyrate, it has been shown to cause minimal suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, which is a critical regulatory system in the body. Clobetasone butyrate is commercially available under the brand names Eumovate and Eumovate, both of which are manufactured by GlaxoSmithKline. Another formulation, Trimovate, combines clobetasone with oxytetracycline, an antibiotic, and nystatin, an antifungal agent. In dermatological applications, clobetasone butyrate is effective in alleviating symptoms such as itching and redness (erythema) associated with eczema and dermatitis. In ophthalmology, 1% clobetasone eye drops have been demonstrated to be both safe and effective in managing dry eye symptoms in patients with Sjögren's Syndrome. Sjögren's Syndrome is an autoimmune disorder that impairs the body's moisture-producing glands, leading to symptoms such as dry eyes. Compared to other corticosteroid eye drops, clobetasone butyrate has been associated with only minimal increases in intraocular pressure, which is a significant advantage as elevated intraocular pressure can lead to glaucoma. Adverse effects associated with the use of clobetasone cream and ointment include sensations of burning, irritation, and itching at the application site. Prolonged use may also result in thinning of the skin and changes in skin pigmentation.
